# SK9095 — An arrangement rule threw and was skipped

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

One rule of the arrangement catalogue raised an exception. That rewrite did not happen; the rest of the catalogue still ran and the file is arranged by the others.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Tool |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Syntax |
| Needs a compilation | no |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

The sibling of `SK9030`, and it exists for the same reason: a rule that throws must cost its own rewrite and nothing else. Before it, an exception out of a rewriter left `Arranger.Arrange` and took the caller with it — the whole report for a nightly fuzz run, the whole process for `skala arrange`. It is a warning rather than a silent skip because "the tool declined to do something and did not say so" is the failure mode the safety layer exists to avoid.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
Func<int> v = new () { P = (from item in items select null) };
```

## When it does not fire

None; it reports an exception that happened. It is a Skala bug even when the throw comes out of a dependency — SK-FUZZ-0012 is Roslyn's own binder throwing `IndexOutOfRangeException` out of a legitimate `GetSymbolInfo` call on a node of the model's own tree.
